primary_reason: The asserted attribute does not exist in any available material: Fu 2020 is paywalled and this study read only abstract-level information; the abstract says only "unique consensus motifs", giving no motif content, frequency or position. The pre-declared estimand requires a binary attribute, and this claim's attribute cannot be read off. Having the site table in hand (paywalled, not redistributed) does not solve it either -- deriving a motif from the site table ourselves and then testing it would test our motif, not the authors' claim, and the attribute would be fixed by the data, violating 'the attribute is written down before the run'.

Observation-channel mismatch, on the same grounds as the phase-2 SFI-004 verdict: this claim comes from a PDB structural survey, so the confounding channel is crystallographic resolvability, not mass-spectrometric peptide visibility, and the pre-declared VIS10/PROT8 cannot describe it by definition. The attribute itself (whether an oxidised Cys's hydrogen-bond partner is Thr or Ser, Arg or Lys) further requires per-structure hydrogen-bond geometry; the supplementary file bi2c00349_si_001.pdf contains only Figures S1-S4, and per-structure hydrogen-bond assignment on 1124 structures was not done in this study.

The claim's structure is 'a set of features has intrinsic discriminative value' (predictor feature validity), not 'a named attribute is enriched in the positive set'. The pre-declared estimand is the log2 odds ratio of a 2x2 table and requires a binary attribute; this claim names no residue or position, and fourteen AAIndex physicochemical properties plus PSAAP form a continuous feature block. Forcing it into a 2x2 would require inventing a threshold, which is a different specification. (Separately noted: Xu 2016's supplementary material was also unreachable this round, but that is not the reason for the verdict.)

Same type as SFE-009: the claim is that 'neighbourhood physicochemical indices predict S-sulfenylation sites', i.e. the overall discriminative power of 2203 features, with no named attribute; n_positive in the claims table is itself blank because the text gives only the feature count. The pre-declared 2x2 odds ratio does not apply to it. (Separately noted: Al-Barakati 2018's supplementary information was also unreachable this round, but that is not the reason for the verdict.)

The asserted attribute is continuous and the authors give no threshold: 'neighbouring-residue SASA over the -10 to -2 segment is higher than at non-SNO sites', with no numbers, no test and no cut-point for 'higher' given in the text. Entering the pre-declared 2x2 would mean inventing a SASA cut-point -- claims like SFE-001 and SNO-002 come with the authors' own cut-points (RSA>25%, RSA>10%); this one does not. Site-level SASA would additionally require structures for this cohort, which were not computed in this study.

Assembling the positive set requires ESI Table S3 of Li 2024 RSC Chem Biol (the list of persulfidated zinc-finger proteins), and all outbound network routes were unavailable this round (the fetch log shows seven requests all failing at SSL handshake, including pypi.org, so this is not a domain-allowlisting problem; no mirror site or spoofed User-Agent was attempted either). The attribute side additionally needs the descendant sets of terms such as GO:0016567/GO:0006511, and QuickGO is equally unreachable; using direct annotations alone would repeat the error already corrected in phase 2. This study holds no substitute persulfidated zinc-finger cohort, so there is no transfer-test route either.

The same paper's ESI (a compilation of zinc-finger types across 22 published persulfidation datasets from 16 studies) is unreachable, and the attribute (CCCC / CCCH / CCHC coordination type) requires a per-protein zinc-finger-type reading that exists only in the authors' ESI and was not reconstructed in this study. The claim is in any case a cross-species comparison, so even with the ESI it would have to be assembled per species.
